chapters.title: A factory full of data but no shared model
Plenty of systems, no shared meaning
What an industrial data model actually is
The model is not the data platform, and why tables alone break down
From PPR to knowledge graphs, ontologies and ISA-95
OPC UA, Asset Administration Shell, digital thread and digital twins
AI, Microsoft Fabric, end-to-end architecture and ownership

takeaways: An industrial data model gives factory objects stable identities, states and relationships across ERP, MES, maintenance and quality without replacing those source systems.
Product, process and resource (PPR) is a practical core structure: it links what the plant builds, how the work must happen and what can perform it under real conditions.
Platforms like Microsoft Fabric, graph databases, digital twins and AI depend on this model and on clear ownership of each definition; they cannot infer factory rules by themselves.
hook: A factory can collect mountains of data and still struggle to answer what a single machine stop really affects. This episode is for manufacturing, IT/OT and data architects who need ERP, MES, maintenance and quality data to share one meaning. Learn how an industrial data model built on product, process and resource links your systems into decision-ready context for planning, digital twins and AI.
